history.summary: Built in 1966 by saint Swami Sewak Das Ji Maharaj (foundation laid 1962), about 2-3.5 km north of Kullu town on the Kullu-Manali highway (NH-21/NH-3) on the banks of the Beas. A small cave enshrines the idol of Goddess Parvati (Vaishno Devi) along with an idol of Durga, and a Shiva temple stands in the complex; managed by Sharda Maa Seva Trust, which runs a free langar, sarai and an acupressure centre. NOTE: this is NOT the famous Katra (J&K) Vaishno Devi shrine; most web image results conflate the two. Festival calendar not documented in consulted sources - Navratri listed as the standard Devi-temple festival (verify). CONFLICT: temple listing reports 5:30 AM-8:00 PM daily; a travel guide reports 8:00 AM-8:00 PM - verify locally. Coordinates from the temple's own listing (31.983243, 77.126291). No reliable on-topic image found after genuine searching - media left empty.

name: Shri Mahadevi Tirth Temple
town_description: Kullu is the district headquarters town in the Kullu valley on the Beas river, ~40 km south of Manali. It is famous for the Kullu Dussehra festival and as the base for travel to Manali, Manikaran and the Parvati valley.

travel.railway: Nearest railheads are distant: narrow-gauge Joginder Nagar and broad-gauge Pathankot/Chandigarh - reach by road
travel.road: On the Kullu-Manali highway (NH-3, old NH-21), 2-3.5 km north of Kullu town; well-connected by bus/taxi

visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:30 AM-8:00 PM daily per temple listing; another guide reports 8:00 AM-8:00 PM - verify locally
